feed.title: Combined summary - PQ-single-address-backup - BIP-38 for P2MR (bc1z) - 104-char encrypted backup format

entry.title: Combined summary - PQ-single-address-backup - BIP-38 for P2MR (bc1z) - 104-char encrypted backup format
entry.summary: The recent discourse in cryptographic security has led to the development of a Post-Quantum single-address backup (PQ-SAB) intended for enhancing the safety of seed storage associated with `bc1z` addresses under BIP-360. This new proposal involves an encrypted paper backup that can safely store seeds against environmental risks such as fire or theft. The PQ-SAB format comprises a base58-encoded payload including a salt, initialization vector, ciphertext, and tag, aggregating to 76 bytes, which equates to 104 characters when encoded using Bitcoin's modified Base58 alphabet. This format employs PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 200,000 iterations for key derivation and AES-256-GCM for encryption. Notably, the seed does not contain a version byte to comply with FIPS-205 and draft specifications of BIP-360, ensuring it remains a pure 32-byte sequence. The implementation strategy necessitates an offline HTML file about 200 lines long, designed to operate without internet connectivity to maintain security during encryption and decryption phases. Each file generates a single `bc1z` address requiring a mandatory password for access, with clear, human-readable details regarding the algorithm, KDF, and encryption visible outside the encrypted portion of the backup. A prototype and documentation are available [in this repository](https://github.com/coldtest-berlin/pq-single-address-backup), along with a live demonstration [here](https://coldtest-berlin.github.io/pq-single-address-backup). Community feedback is currently sought to potentially standardize this 104-character encrypted backup alongside BIP-360. Further advancements in blockchain protocols include significant updates to BIP-360, notably removing specific prefixes like bc1z and bc1r as of August 14, 2026. This modification serves to keep the format neutral and adaptable, supporting both P2MR and P2QRH types without embedding any previous prefix constraints. The seed configuration sustains a robust security protocol by maintaining a pure 32-byte SLH-DSA structure, enhancing the flexibility and longevity of the protocol responsive to technological progress and user input. Additionally, recent enhancements in cryptographic payload formats emphasize the importance of self-describing binary payloads for wallet interoperability and recovery operations. The inclusion of clear identifiers like version numbers and algorithm specifications within the payload is essential for wallets to accurately process different profiles and detect incorrect wrappers. The upcoming Version 2 will introduce internal restructuring where versioning information will be integrated within the authenticated payload, facilitating a more reliable decoding process capable of rejecting mismatched wrappers due to unsupported versions or incorrect passwords while maintaining essential human-readable hints. This restructuring also includes plans for integrating a checksum within a fixed 104-character encoding to aid pre-key derivation function typo detection, enhancing both security and user experience for long-lived paper backups. Lastly, a proposed method to enhance digital wallet security through an encrypted backup format suitable for Post-Quantum Cryptography involves a minimal outer header in the encryption schema containing crucial elements like format version and KDF identifier, which assists in pre-decryption processes. This method aims to use Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) to indicate authentication failures rather than verifying password or ciphertext integrity directly, addressing potential transcription errors preemptively. The proposed standard aims for wide adoption, potentially under a shared Bitcoin Improvement Proposal that supports a pure 32-byte seed, prefix-agnostic and compatible with BIP-360, ensuring a standardized approach across various platforms.
